text: The moon hangs low and heavy over the Sierra Nevada peaks, its pale light casting long, jagged shadows across the frozen riverbeds where the gold seekers have made their desperate camps. This celestial witness to the American gold rush illuminates a world defined by raw adventure, acute risk, and the unyielding pursuit of wealth and survival. In this novel, the moon serves not just as a natural satellite, but as a silent, cold observer of the human spirit pushed to its absolute limits, reflecting the stark beauty and brutal reality of the frontier.
